# अर्जुनः (Arjunah)

> A browser extension and open protocol that lets a website use the AI its visitor already has. The extension injects window.ai.arjunah into every page; the site publishes an assistant contract (level 0) or enables access and calls the visitor's chosen model (level 1 or 2). The visitor approves per exact origin; the site never sees credentials, accounts, or quotas.

Names: everything a person sees says अर्जुनः; code, packages, and identifiers use arjunah. npm: arjunah (TypeScript SDK and types for sites), arjunah-widget (the same chat widget mounted against your own backend, without the wallet guarantees; its bridged mode answers your loop with the visitor's model through the extension), arjunah-desktop (desktop companion that lends Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode subscriptions). Visitor providers: OpenAI, OpenCode Zen, Ollama Cloud (API keys), a self-hosted Ollama server (provider kind "self-hosted"), and desktop subscriptions; check each model's capabilities. Page API: window.ai.arjunah with isEnabled(), enable() (defaults to level 1, resolves to a session carrying models, conversations, providers, context, permissions; require: { kinds, local, builtinTools } restricts which visitor models may answer), disable(), openSettings() (user gesture only), site.register(), chat.*, and the window event arjunah:grantchange. Model entries and results carry kind, local, and builtinTools; generate accepts toolChoice, and models.stream / conversation.stream answer the same round as an async iterable of bounded deltas ending in the same result. Levels say only how far the visitor's model reaches; who composes the conversation (extension, site server, or page) and who draws it (extension or page) picks one of five modes.

## Integrate a website

- [Integration guide](docs/INTEGRATION.md): the API on one screen, level choice, manifest bounds, generate request and result, error codes, traps, how to verify locally. Start here.
- [The five modes](docs/INTEGRATION.md#the-five-modes): who composes and who draws, one minimal example each (extension loop, a server or page loop in the extension's panel, a server loop behind the widget, a page loop). Read before choosing between site.register and a loop of your own; SPEC section 15 is the normative table.
- [Tool loops and reasoning continuity](docs/INTEGRATION.md#tool-loops-and-reasoning-continuity): one conversation per thread (conversations.create / open / release), provider state kept between tool rounds, desktop agent sessions reused; the section before it streams a round with models.stream or conversation.stream.
- [SDK types](packages/sdk/src/types.ts): every request and result shape, with the limits in doc comments.
- [SDK entry point](packages/sdk/src/index.ts): the helpers the arjunah package exports.
- [Paint playground](demo/paint/index.html): the primary level-0 example, including structured text/image tool results.
- [Trip planner](demo/trip-planner/index.html): the original level 0, 1, and 2 integration.
- [Standalone widget](packages/widget/README.md): mounting the chat against your own backend, the SSE event stream, thread routes, card actions, the built-in model picker, `@` entity mentions, tool inputs the model never sees, approvals, bridged mode (your loop's model.client answered by the visitor's model through the extension), and the in-page backend (backend.fetch: your page runs the loop, no network request from the widget).
- [Test fixture](tests/fixtures/site.html): minimal registrations used by the browser suites.

## Protocol

- [Specification](SPEC.md): normative. Sections 1 (actors, roles), 3 (discovery), 4 (levels, require, consent), 5.3 (generation, content parts, toolChoice, round streaming), 5.4 (conversations and provider state), 7 (site contracts, schema subset, widget, collected inputs, transcript cards, tool progress, site-owned threads, declared remote tools, approvals), 8.2 and 8.3 (the renderer's model picker and entity mentions), 9 (errors), 14 (standalone renderer, bridged mode in 14.7), 15 (roles and the five modes, hosted external loop, the site's own models, consent per mode).
- [Security model](SECURITY.md): what stays in the extension, what the page can never see.

## Install and run

- [Install guide](docs/INSTALL.md): extension for Chrome and Firefox, desktop companion for macOS, Linux, Windows.
- [Desktop companion](docs/DESKTOP.md): pairing, autostart, provider states, subscription agents.
